papers.title_en: Signal Scaffolding: Unlocking the Potential of Lightweight Models for Self-Supervised Monocular Depth Estimation
papers.authors: Zhijie Wang, Li Zhang, Yujie Chen, Shibiao Deng, Xin Gao, Houzhi Zhou, Jiangshuo Zhang
papers.evidence: 面向边缘设备的轻量级自监督单目深度估计
papers.tldr: 轻量自监督单目深度估计在边缘设备需求下发展迅速，但现有方法精度普遍不足。作者认为瓶颈在于常规训练未能充分释放轻量模型潜力，提出三阶段训练策略Signal Scaffolding，并将其用于自设计网络ReForgeDepth。在KITTI和Cityscapes上，该方法取得精度-效率权衡的领先表现，并可在边缘设备实时运行。这表明无需增加数据或参数，通过改进训练即可挖掘轻量模型的潜在能力。
papers.abstract_en: With the rising demand for edge devices, lightweight self-supervised monocular depth estimation methods have continued to evolve; however, existing methods generally suffer from poor accuracy. We find that the root cause may lies in the failure of conventional training regimes to fully exploit the inherent potential of lightweight models. To address this, we propose a novel three-phase training strategy for lightweight self-supervised monocular depth estimation, termed Signal Scaffolding (SS). Without introducing any additional dataset or parameters, we apply SS to ReForgeDepth, a lightweight network of our own design. Experiments on the KITTI and Cityscapes datasets demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance in the accuracy-efficiency trade-off and running in real time on edge devices. These results suggest that lightweight models can be improved further within their existing capacity, and that the central question may be less about how parameters are allocated than about how to unlock this latent potential through training.

papers.title_en: Zoom In, Scale Out: Metric Depth Models Mistake Digital Zoom for Moving Closer
papers.evidence: 诊断Depth Anything V2在数字变焦下的度量深度与焦距行为
papers.tldr: 单目度量深度模型要从一张照片估计米制距离，还必须隐式判断拍摄相机；数字变焦不改变场景距离，是检验这一能力的免费精确测试。作者将图像裁剪放大回原尺寸，用缩放因子拟合深度与焦距的幂律反应。Depth Anything V2的α=0.95，几乎把变焦误判为相机靠近；带相机预测的模型仅部分缓解。给定真实相机后Depth Pro等能保持深度，说明误差在相机估计；无标签修正使Depth Pro的α降至0.04，并揭示模型依赖物体表观大小的捷径。
papers.abstract_en: Many new AI models estimate how far away things are, in metres, from a single photo. To do this they must also work out what camera took the photo. We check whether they really do with a simple test: digital zoom, that is, cropping a photo and enlarging the crop back to full size. Zooming moves nothing in the scene, so a correct model should give the same distance for every point still in the picture. The test is free, exact and needs no labels. Two numbers describe a model's reaction: its depth changes like $s^{-α}$ (ideal $α=0$) and its focal-length estimate like $s^β$ (ideal $β=1$), for zoom factor $s$. On 800 images from KITTI, NYUv2 and DIODE, the widely used Depth Anything V2 has $α=0.95$: it treats a zoomed photo almost as if the camera had moved closer, because it judges distance mainly from how large things look. Models that also predict the camera remove only part of this error ($α\approx0.31$-$0.36$), because their focal estimate grows too little. Given the true camera, Depth Pro and DA3-Nested keep their depth ($α\approx0$), so the error lies in their camera estimate. The reason: a zoomed photo is, pixel for pixel, a normal photo of a scene squashed in depth, so size alone cannot tell the two apart, and a focal estimator trained by regression stays close to the cameras it saw in training. Undoing this needs no labels or training and makes Depth Pro pass the test ($α=0.04$) at almost no cost on normal photos. Controls, including a real optical zoom lens, rule out blur and resizing artefacts. Finally, label-free fine-tuning for self-consistency lowers $α$ to 0.05 on KITTI and 0.07 on NYUv2 once a "blurry means zoomed" shortcut is removed; we report what this costs on normal and unseen photos.

papers.title_en: Calibrating the Uncertainty of Self-Supervised Monocular Depth without Labels
papers.evidence: 无标签的自监督单目深度不确定性校准
papers.tldr: 自监督单目深度网络能预测逐像素不确定性，但现有评价只看排序质量，不检查不确定度数值是否与真实深度误差相当。论文先系统检验KITTI上不确定性的尺度与形状校准，发现所有方法均尺度失准，MonoProb的误差约为其预测不确定度的两倍。为此提出MonoCal：用立体图像对估计一个常数做尺度校准且无需重训练，再通过第二自监督网络的深度分歧重训练以修正形状。实验表明其在各不确定度水平和深度范围上校准优于用真值重缩放，推理仍只需单张图像。
papers.abstract_en: Self-supervised monocular depth networks can predict a per-pixel uncertainty, which is mainly evaluated by how well it ranks pixels according to their error. Such metrics are insensitive to the magnitude of the uncertainty, so an uncertainty half as large as the actual error obtains the same score. In this paper, we investigate whether the predicted uncertainty is as large as the depth error, both on average (scale) and across confident and uncertain, near and far pixels (shape). On KITTI, the scale is miscalibrated for every uncertainty estimate we evaluate, and the error of MonoProb is nearly twice its predicted uncertainty. We propose MonoCal, which corrects both the scale and the shape without ground-truth depth. Scale calibration multiplies the uncertainty by a single constant measured from stereo pairs, requiring no retraining, and this constant closely matches the one fitted with ground truth. Since a constant cannot change the shape, we further retrain the uncertainty to predict where the depth of the network disagrees with that of a second self-supervised network. Experiments on KITTI show that MonoCal achieves better calibration across uncertainty levels and depth ranges than rescaling with ground truth, while still using a single image at inference. Code will be made publicly available.
